questions.q: A water drop of diameter <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is broken into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>64</mn></math> equal droplets. The surface tension of water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>075</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. In this process the gain in surface energy will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By conserving the total volume 43πR3=64×43πr3⇒R=4r

Change in surface energy is

ΔU=T×ΔA, =T64×4πr2-4πR2

=4πTR264×116-1=12×3.14×0.075×10-4

≈2.8×10-4 J

questions.q: A fluid is flowing through a horizontal pipe of varying cross-section, with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi><mtext> </mtext><msup><mi>ms</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at a point where the pressure is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> Pascal. At another point where pressure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> Pascal its speed is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>ms</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If the density of the fluid is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">ρ</mi><mtext> </mtext><mi>kg</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> and the flow is streamline, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is equal to
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
P+12ρv2=P2+12ρV2

P2+12ρv2=12ρV2 ;

V=v2+Pρ

questions.q: A solid sphere, of radius R acquires a terminal velocity <math><msub><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> when falling (due to gravity) through a viscous fluid having a coefficient of viscosity <math><mi>η</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The sphere is broken into 27 identical solid spheres. If each of these spheres acquires a terminal velocity, <math><msub><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> when falling through the same fluid, the ratio <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math> equals:

questions.solution:
If R is the radius of initial drop and r is the radius of new drop, then
43πR3=27×43πr3⇒r=R3
Terminal velocity,

         vT∝r2
⇒ v1v2=R2R32=9

questions.q: The height of liquid column raised in a capillary tube of certain radius when dipped in liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> vertically is, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. If the tube is dipped in a similar manner in another liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> of surface tension and density double the values of liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>, the height of liquid column raised in liquid B would be ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The height h through which a liquid will rise in a capillary tube of radius r is given by,

h=2Tcosθrρg∝Tρ∝2T2ρ

As we can see in both cases, value of height will remain same. Therefore,

h'=h=5 cm= 0.05 m

Excess pressure at common surface is given by

questions.q: A big drop is formed by coalescing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn></math> small droplets of water. The surface energy will become :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Lets say radius of small droplets is r and that of big drop is R. Total volume of the drops will remains unchanged. Therefore, 

43πR3=100043πr3

⇒R=10r

Now, initial surface energy is, Ui=10004πr2 S and the final surface energy is, 

Uf=4πR2 S

=1004πr2S

Clearly, Uf=110Ui.

Balancing the forces on drop 

Buoyant force + surface tension =mg

σV2g+2πRT=ρVg

⇒R3=3T2ρ-σg⇒R=3×7.5×10-2 N-m-12ρ-σ×10

R=3202ρ-σ m=152ρ-σ cm

Work done to increase the radius of soap bubble from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> will be : [Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>22</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></math> ]

As we know,

Work done = change in surface energy of soap bubble

Therefore,

Work done =2T4πr22-4πr12

=18.48×10-4J

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : When a capillary tube is dipped into a liquid, the liquid neither rises nor falls in the capillary. The contact angle may be $0^{\circ}$.
Statement II : The contact angle between a solid and a liquid is a property of the material of the solid and liquid as well.
In the light of the above statement, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Capillary rise
$\mathrm{h}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~T} \cos \theta}{\rho \mathrm{gr}} \text {; }$
If $\theta=0^{\circ}$ then rise is non-zero
$\therefore$ Statement-1 is incorrect.

questions.q: Two spherical soap bubbles of radii <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> in vacuum combine under isothermal conditions. The resulting bubble has a radius equal to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Excess of pressure, inside the first bubble
$p_1=\frac{4 T}{r_1}$
Similarly, $\quad p_2=\frac{4 T}{r_2}$
Let the radius of the large bubble be $R$.
Then, excess of pressure inside the large bubble,
$p=\frac{4 T}{R}$
Under isothermal condition, temperature remains constant.
So, $\quad P V=p_1 V_1+p_2 V_2\frac{4 T}{R}\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3\right)=\frac{4 T}{r_1}\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi r_1^3\right)+\frac{4 T}{r_2}\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi r_2^3\right)R^2=r_1^2+r_2^2\Rightarrow \quad R=\sqrt{r_1^2+r_2^2}$

questions.q: Two water drops each of radius 'r' coalesce to from a bigger drop. If ' T ' is the surface tension, the surface energy released in this process is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 2 \times \frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3=\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{r}^3 \Rightarrow \mathrm{r}=2^{1 / 3} \mathrm{R} \\ & \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=2 \times 4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{~T} \\ & \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{f}}=4 \pi \mathrm{r}^2 \mathrm{~T}=4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{~T} 2^{2 / 3} \\ & \therefore \text { Heat lost }=\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{f}}=4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{~T}\left[2-2^{2 / 3}\right]\end{aligned}$

It is observed that the two tangents drawn from observed that the two tangents drawn from liquid-glass interfaces (from opp. sides of the capillary) make an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>º</mo></math> with one another. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></math> is close to (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
h=2Tcosθρgr  θ=30°  P=667 kg m-3; T=1/20 N m-1; r=0.15×10-3

=2×120×32667×10×0.15×10-3=0.087m

questions.q: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble is thrice the excess pressure inside a second soap bubble. The ratio between the volume of the first and the second bubble is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\mathrm{P}_1-\mathrm{P}_0=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_1} \qquad \quad \quad \quad\mathrm{P}_2-\mathrm{P}_0=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_2}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}_1-\mathrm{P}_0=3\left(\mathrm{P}_2-\mathrm{P}_0\right) \\ & \frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_1}=3 \frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_2} \\ & \mathrm{r}_2=3 \mathrm{r}_1 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{V}_1}{\mathrm{~V}_2}=\frac{\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{r}_1^3}{\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{r}_2^3}=\frac{1}{27}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A mercury drop of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is broken into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>125</mn></math> equal size droplets. Surface tension of mercury is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>45</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> . questions.solution:
As the volume of the mercury will remain same, therefore

43πR3=12543πr3⇒R=5r

Now, increase in surface energy

∆U=125×S×4πr2-S×4πR2

 =0.45×4π×10-3212525-1

=4×0.45×4π×10-6

=2.26×10-5J

questions.q: The ratio of surface tensions of mercury and water is given to be <math><mn>7.5</mn></math>, while the ratio of their densities is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>13.6</mn></math>. Their contact angles, with glass, are close to <math><mn>135</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, respectively. If it is observed that mercury gets depressed by an amount <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> in a capillary tube of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>, while water rises by the same amount <math><mi>h</mi></math> in a capillary tube of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, then the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> is close to
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
|hHg|=|hwater|

2S1cosθ1ρ1r1g=2S2cosθ2ρ2r2g

Therefore, the ratio of the radii of the respective tubes is,

r1r2=ρ2ρ1×S1cosθ1S2cosθ2

r1r2=113.6×7.5×12

r1r2≈25

questions.q: Pressure inside two soap bubbles are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>02</mn></math> atmosphere, respectively. The ratio of their volumes is :

questions.solution:
Excess pressure inside a soap bubble is 4TR. Therefore,

P1-P0=4TR1=0.01 atm

P2-P0=4TR2=0.02 atm

Dividing,

12=R2R1

⇒R1=2R2

⇒V1V2=R13R23=8R23R23=81

questions.q: A large number of water drops, each of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math>, combine to have a drop of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>. If the surface tension is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi></math> and mechanical equivalent of heat is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>J</mi></math>, the rise in heat energy per unit volume will be:

n×43πr3=43πR3

∴ n1/3r=R

∴ Total change in surface energy

=n4πr2-4πR2T

⇒4πTnr2-R2

∴ Heat energy

=4πTnr2-R2J×43πR3=3 T Jnr2R3-1R

questions.q: A hydraulic press containing water has two arms with diameters as mentioned in the figure. A force of $10 \mathrm{~N}$ is applied on the surface of water in the thinner arm. The force required to be applied on the surface of water in the thicker arm to maintain equilibrium of water is _____N.

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{F_1}{A_1}=\frac{F_2}{A_2} \\ & \frac{F_1}{\pi(7)^2}=\frac{10}{\pi \times(0.7)^2} \\ & F_1=1000 \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Consider a water tank as shown in the figure. It's cross-sectional area is 0.4 m2. The tank has an opening B near the bottom whose cross-section area is 1 cm2. A load of 24 kg is applied on the water at the top when the height of the water level is 40 cm above the bottom, the velocity of water coming out the opening B is v m s-1. The value of v, to the nearest integer, is ___ .[Take the value of g to be 10 m s-2]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
m=24 kg

A=0.4 m2

a=1 cm2

H=40 cm

Using Bernoulli's equation, 

⇒P0+mgA+ρgH+12Pv12

=P0+0+12ρv2   ...1

⇒ Neglecting v1

⇒v=2gH+2mgAρ

⇒v=8+1.2

⇒v=3.033 m s-1

⇒v≃3 m s-1

questions.q: A spherical soap bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is formed inside another spherical soap bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. If the internal pressure of the smaller bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> in the above system is equal to the internal pressure of the another single soap bubble of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> is _____
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Pressure inside a bubble is given by, P0+4Tr.

Pressure inside the bubble of smaller radius will be, 

P2-P1=P0+4T6+4T3

Pressure inside the bubble with radius r, P0+4Tr

Now,

⇒P0+4T6+4T3=P0+4Tr

⇒1r=16+13

⇒r=2 cm

questions.q:
A spherical ball of radius 1 mm and density 10.5 g cc-1 is dropped in glycerine of coefficient of viscosity 9.8 poise and density 1.5 g cc-1. Viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity is 3696×10-x N. The value of x is

(Given, g=9.8 m s-2 and π=227)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity i.e., terminal velocity is,

 Fv=mg-FB  As, a=0

Here, FB is buoyant force.

⇒Fv=Vρbg-Vρgg=Vgρb-ρg=43π10-33×9.810.5-1.5×103≈3696×10-7 N

Thus, x=7.

questions.q: A thin transparent film with refractive index 1.4 , is held on circular ring of radius 1.8 cm . The fluid in the film evaporates such that transmission through the film at wavelength 560 nm goes to a minimum every 12 seconds. Assuming that the film is flat on its two sides, the rate of evaporation is ____ $\pi \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~m}^3 / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a thin film interference, a fringe for transmission is formed.
When
$2 \mu x=n \lambda\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \frac{d x}{d t}=\left(\frac{d n}{d t}\right) \frac{\lambda}{2 \mu} \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{12}\right) \frac{560 \times 10^{-9}}{2 \times 1.4}=\frac{5}{3} \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & V=\text { Volume of film }=\pi R^2 x \\ & \frac{d V}{d t}=\pi R^2 \frac{d x}{d t} \\ & =\pi\left(1.8 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \frac{5}{3} \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~m}^3 / \mathrm{s} \\ & =54 \pi \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~m}^3 / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$
